anchor_definition: The anchor is double_submit: the login submit handler whose body reads #pwd/#un, constructs a JSEncrypt, sets the public key, RSA-encrypts password (and username) inline, and assembles the credentials.* payload it posts. PLAN section 4.3: the password ciphertext is constructed inline inside this function (no dedicated encrypt function), so this enclosing function is the anchor; PLAN section 5.1: not the validation precondition it calls, a cookie util, or the JSEncrypt library primitive. There is no separate 0.7 target-specific helper because the target-specific construction is inline in double_submit.

anchor.why: Builds the login request: new JSEncrypt + setPublicKey(pubkey), j=i.encrypt(password), then h={'credentials.password':j,...} which is posted to /publicPassport/login.do. This constructs the exact credentials.password value observed.

roles.why: Generic JSEncrypt public API used by the anchor for both password and username. It delegates to the RSA key and base64-encodes the ciphertext, but does not bind the result to credentials.password.
Generic key-loading wrapper called by the anchor before encryption. It binds a key object for the library, not the target request field.
Generic RSA encrypt routine below JSEncrypt.encrypt. It applies PKCS#1 padding and public-key exponentiation but is reusable library code.
Generic PKCS#1 v1.5 padding helper that introduces random padding before RSA. It explains non-determinism but not the credentials.password binding.
Generic public-key modular exponentiation called by the RSA encrypt path.
Generic hex-to-base64 formatter used by JSEncrypt.encrypt to return the ciphertext string.
Validation gate called by the submit handler before encryption (checks the account and password fields). On the path but does not construct the encrypted value.
Enter-key handler that clicks #login_button and reaches the submit flow. It is an upstream trigger, not the encryption constructor.
Configures the slide captcha and calls double_submit on validation success. It is path-critical for the slider branch but does not derive credentials.password.
Generic jQuery shorthand used by the login request. It forwards already prepared data to ajax and does not encrypt the password.
Generic network sink reached after double_submit has already constructed the encrypted credentials.password field.
Response callback for /publicPassport/login.do. It handles errors/redirects after the request has already been sent.
A generic cookie reader utility; unrelated to the password encryption path.
A second cookie reader used by validation-code initialization. Cookie-looking helper but off the RSA password construction path.
Checks whether a username/mobile account needs password completion. It posts credentials.username only and is not the login password encryption path.
QR-code login flow helper. It uses passport endpoints but does not construct credentials.password.

empty_roles.why: No separate complete target-specific helper exists: double_submit itself reads #pwd, sets the RSA public key, encrypts the password, and writes credentials.password inline. Downstream helpers are generic RSA/JSEncrypt utilities (0.5), and upstream triggers are path-critical (0.2).

do_not_promote: The exact anchor is double_submit because the target-specific password read, key binding, RSA encrypt call and credentials.password payload assignment are all inline there.
There is no legitimate 0.7 nested target-specific helper; JSEncrypt/RSA functions are generic primitives and stay at 0.5.
checkAccountAndPwdForLogin, doEnter and initSlideCaptcha are on the path but do not construct the encrypted password.
jQuery get/post/ajax and the login response callback emit or process an already prepared request.
The username ciphertext is a same-request sibling field and should not be treated as the requested credentials.password observable.
Cookie readers, account-type checks, QR-code login and captcha helpers are off-chain decoys.
oracle_notes.offset_convention: All offsets are 0-based UTF-16 code-unit indices over the BOM-stripped UTF-8 text. sha256 is over the UTF-8 bytes of the slice. This differs from the synthetic suite's response_schema wording ("byte offset"); both graders slice by their own convention.
audit_notes: Answer match check: 1.json case 19 code is a contiguous snippet inside double_submit, and oracle.primary_anchor is double_submit.

Question direction check: the visible question asks for the complete function whose own body reads #pwd, RSA-encrypts it with the public key and assembles credentials.password; this points to double_submit.

No valid role in this case; the target-specific construction is inline in double_submit.
